title: Dope addiction on the old corner
summary: Addiction was less common then; he saw addicts start at his corner for 21 years.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, did they take junk in those days? Did those fellas take junk in those days? Oh, yeah. They had junk back then. That's a terrible thing. I guess it was killing them off then like it was killing them all.

It wasn't as many. It wasn't as many them days as it is today. I lived over there 21 years at that corner house, with my wife. And I saw 95% of the dope addicts around here start off right on that corner. I know boys from a good family, swell boys. And I, you see, they had them big old doves. They'd keep them on the jaw like that. Of course, I'd have the light out. It'd be dark. And they're sitting on them. I step out of them sniff cocaine. I saw them shoot the needle right on that corner over there. See, on this side they had a big shed all the way around. And where the people lived upstairs, what they used to call them, Ferraros was their name. They lived upstairs. They had about three or four daughters and one son. Tony's one son, and they had three or four daughters. And when they'd close the place at night, those guys would get on those steps and shoot the needle. And you could see them, they'd take a beer top. And I don't know how they could do it and heat it. I guess it'd make it watery like when shoot the needle. That house there, Newhouse now, it was old how they? Right across the street? Yeah. Not that one next to it. Newhouse was pretty little old. I see many of them guys right up there. Kill them dead. Kill them dead. Overdose. I used to be out in the French quarters with the Sy brothers, Sam, Tony, and Russell, and all that side gang. Well, I used to be out there with those guys.
